title: backlog.py new runs a bug's repro once and refuses one that fails by a Python error rather than its exit code
goal: backlog.py new bug (and set --repro, and land's checks) refuses a repro, naming the exception class, when it ends in an uncaught TypeError, NameError or UnboundLocalError raised in its own code (the -c string or an untracked script), which says the repro's code is wrong rather than the defect; an error on a value the code under test returned (an AttributeError on its None, ST-4mdnjuep's contract), one raised inside the code under test and an AssertionError stay accepted. A planted repro calling a function with the wrong arguments is refused, one that exits 1 by sys.exit is accepted. Retrospective of SP-smqwmchu: BG-nf6gcqsz was filed with a repro that failed by TypeError, not by the defect.
